events.body:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the refund base is this trip's own per-km rate, distance fare ÷ distance km: $13.55 ÷ 9.61 km = $1.4100/km [F6][F9][RD-2]. Segment 14:10–14:15 (F4): the trace settles RD-4(a) as satisfied — an Accident on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road, two lanes closed, reported 13:52, on the optimal route, i.e. before the segment start and within the route corridor [F18][F15][RD-4]. That is a reasonable cause for substituting the stretch of the optimal route being driven, and Orchard Road was at band 1 (0–9 km/h) over 14:00–14:10, i.e. when the driver set off [F15][RD-4]. (14:02), the driver's "Ok" (14:03), all timestamped — and the driver's post-trip statement and the complaint [F10][F11][F12][F13][F14]. claims.assertion: The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride, so detour kilometres flow straight into the fare: the taxi ran 9.6 km against a 3.9 km optimal route (+5.7 km, +144%) and the fare bills 9.61 km of distance ($13.55), so metered distance is the refund base under RD-2.

Segment 14:10–14:15 added 1.85 km of unmetered-route distance (2.68 km driven vs 0.83 km of optimal route) and is not covered by the rider's consent: the rider's only reply (F11, 14:02) granted a general route choice plus a stop request, and it precedes the segment start at 14:10.

Even if the 14:10–14:15 segment were treated as the agreed 'go round by Cavenagh' route, the driver's own claimed course must hold: the chat contains no message tying any driven segment to Cavenagh Road and no road-name fact ties the segment to it, so on the named-road reading the segment is undetermined, not exempt (this does not stop the driver's own traffic record from mitigating it).

The driver's accident/congestion excuse fails on its own record: the accident on Orchard Road is reported at 0 m from the sub-optimal 3.9 km route (F18) and Orchard Road's band-1 congestion (F15) runs only 14:00–14:10, whereas the deviation continues to 14:29 and the excess distance is billed for the whole detour — so on RD-4 the justification touches the old route, not the driven one.

The rider consented only to a stop 'on the way' (F11), never to a stop at Beach Road and never to an off-route diversion; the driver's post-trip statement that he chose the Beach Road 7-Eleven (F14) is a claim, and the resulting stay is a system record: 4 min 10 s stationary at 14:20–14:24, 2,995 m from pickup and 2,098 m from drop-off, i.e. not on the way at all.

The second off-route segment 14:17–14:29 added 2.87 km (3.64 km driven vs 0.77 km optimal, straying up to 1,553 m from the optimal route) and remains wholly unexplained and uncovered by any consent message earlier than 14:17, so it is an unexempted detour under RD-1/RD-5.

The two off-route segments together account for 1.85 + 2.87 = 4.72 km of excess distance; at this trip's own per-km rate of $1.4100/km (F6, = fare.distance_fare $13.55 ÷ fare.distance_km 9.61) that is $6.6552, rounded to $6.66, which is the RD-2 refund figure (the unbilled remainder of the fare excess beyond the segments is not recoverable).
The $1.08 waiting charge is metered wait time (F7) and, being RydeTAXI, is collectable per the meter and not refundable under RD-3(c); the rider does not seek it.

The driver has 1 upheld dispute in the last 90 days (F21, a no-show matter, route: 0), so this case does not meet RD-6's 'route_disputes_upheld_90d >= 1' condition and no flag_account is requested; the profile is cited only as history, never to prove this detour.

No safety escalation is warranted on this record: the chat is complete and every message is timestamped, there is no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in the messages (F10–F13), and the driver's statement is civil in tone (F14), so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 are not engaged.

weaknesses: The rider's own message F11 ('Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?') is a general route authorization and a stop request; the driver will argue under RD-3(a)/(b) and RD-5 that the whole 14:10–14:15 diversion was the agreed 'go round by Cavenagh' and that the 4 min 10 s at F2 was merely the rider-requested stop, so the judge may exempt at least that segment (or find it undetermined under G13, sending it to a human), cutting the $6.66 claim.

F15 (Orchard Road band 1, 0–9 km/h, 14:00–14:10) and F18 (accident at 13:52, 0 m from the optimal route) are genuine RD-4(a) traffic facts; the driver will rely on them to argue 'reasonable cause' for the first segment, even though they support the sub-optimal Orchard route the driver abandoned rather than the 5 km of driving actually undertaken.

The 14:17–14:29 segment is time-stamped before no consent exists at all, but the chat (F11) does not name any road for it, so part of the detour is argued from absence of consent rather than an affirmative record; the rider also cannot show the driver was told the stop must be a specific shop, and F2's 4 min 10 s at 2,995 m from pickup is the only hard proof of the off-route stop.
The $1.08 wait (F7) is metered time on a RydeTAXI trip and is collectable under RD-3(c); the rider accepts it, which shortens the refund the rider can ask for.

Refund would be issued as a Ryde voucher, not cash (NS-7), and F6's excess-distance line is a fare-system conversion, so the judge must accept $1.4100/km as this trip's rate rather than a separately published per-km tariff (G10).

claims.assertion: The trip was a RydeTAXI metered trip (F9 shows base/distance/time/waiting components, not a fixed quote), so any refund is limited to the metered mileage units of off-route segments and must be computed from the per-km rate $13.55 ÷ 9.61 km = $1.4100/km (F6, F9).

Segment 1 (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km, F4) is exempt under RD-4: the incident fact F18 records an Accident on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road with two lanes closed, reported 13:52, 0 m from the optimal route and before the segment started; F15 confirms Orchard Road was at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 14:00–14:10 and F19 shows fair weather (no alternative explanation).

Segment 1 is additionally covered by the rider's own prior consent: the driver proposed the Cavenagh routing at 14:01 (F10) and the rider replied 'Sure' at 14:02 (F11), before the segment began at 14:10 (F4), which is a general route authorization covering the route chosen to reach the destination (RD-5).

As to Segment 2 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, F5), the rider asked for 'a 7-Eleven on the way' (F11) but named no location, and the driver states he chose the 7-Eleven on Beach Road (F14) — a place ~1.5 km off the optimal route (F5); because the rider's request named no place, her consent was to 'a stop', not to that routing, and the segment is not exempt (RD-3(b), RD-5).

The driver's written claim that the rider agreed verbally and that it was the same Cavenagh deal (F14) is a statement, not consent, and cannot extend the 14:02 message (F11) to the Beach Road segment F5, since that message never named Beach Road.

The stationary period 14:20–14:24 of 4 min 10 s at 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off (F2) falls inside Segment 2 and is the 7-Eleven stop; it is a stop on a non-exempt segment and the only disclosed stop charge is the $5.00 pick-up waiting fee, so the billed waiting time of $1.08 (F7) must be treated as mileage-neutral but the driver does not contest it; no $3.00 destination change applies.

The refund should be partial and limited to the non-exempt Segment 2 mileage only: 2.87 km × $1.4100/km = $4.05 (computed from the extra_km in F5 and the per-km rate in F6/F9), leaving the rest of the metered fare (F9) standing; the total charged $25.81 (F9) should not be refunded in full.

No account flag is warranted: the driver has one upheld dispute in 90 days and that single upheld matter is a no-show, not a route deviation (F21 route: 0), so RD-6's 'repeated route deviation' condition is not met even though his 812 trips and 4.7 rating (F21) show no pattern of mileage abuse.

No safety escalation is triggered: the chat consists of the driver's route question, the rider's 'Sure' and stop request, and the driver's 'Ok' (F10–F12), with no threat, intimidation or harassment in any message or in the complaint.

weaknesses: The raw numbers are bad for the driver: actual 9.6 km against a 3.9 km optimal route, +5.7 km or +144% (F1), and duration 26.5 min against 7.7 min estimated (F3); on total distance the trip looks like an obvious detour.

Segment 2 is only defensible if the judge accepts that the rider's 'stop at a 7-Eleven on the way' (F11) somehow covered Beach Road; the driver's own statement (F14) shows the location was his choice, and the stop was 1553 m from the optimal route (F5, F2) — under RD-3(b)/RD-5 this segment is almost certainly non-exempt, so a partial refund is the realistic best case.

There is no record tying the driven Segment 2 to any road the rider named — she never named Beach Road — so on consent the segment is at best undetermined (G13) and at worst fully chargeable to the driver.

The speed-band 4 on Bras Basah Road (F16) and band 3 on Bayfront Avenue (F17) do not help: RD-4(b) says a band fact alone does not exempt a segment, and the driver never claimed congestion on those roads.

points.response: Accepted — we agree the ride is metered RydeTAXI and that the per-km rate is fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km = $13.55 ÷ 9.61 = $1.4100/km (F6, F9); the only live issue is which segments are exempt, not the rate.

The RD-4(a) exemption is route-specific: F18 places the accident 0 m from the 3.9 km optimal route (Orchard Road towards Bras Basah) and F15 puts band-1 congestion on Orchard Road only for 14:00–14:10, so they justify substituting the old route, not driving the driven course of 14:10–14:29 that adds 4.72 km (F4, F5); the exemption at most mitigates the segment the incident actually covers, and F19's fair weather is neutral.

Even on the general-authorization reading, F11 ('Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?') at 14:02 covers only the route chosen for the journey — it cannot cover a 5 km loop and a 2,995 m trip to a shop (F1, F2), and on the named-road reading RD-5 requires a record tying the 14:10–14:15 segment to Cavenagh Road, of which there is none, so the segment is undetermined at best; the longest off-route reach is 1,553 m in F5, not the 803 m of F4.

We agree Segment 2 is non-exempt, but on the rider's side of RD-3(b): the driver himself concedes the rider named no place and that Beach Road was his own choice (F14), and F2 shows the stop 2,995 m from pickup and 2,098 m from drop-off — nowhere 'on the way' — so the rider's 'stop on the way' request (F11) cannot exempt it; the full 2.87 km of F5 stands payable to the rider.

Agreed and it cuts both ways: the driver's post-trip statement (F14) is a claim that cannot extend consent (G11 reasoning in RD-5), and by the same rule it cannot turn F11 into agreement to a Beach Road run — so no part of F5 is consensual.

The $1.08 (F7) is metered waiting time on a RydeTAXI trip and is collectable per RD-3(c) — but note the driver's own admission that his chosen stop was 1,553 m off the optimal route (F5) and 2,995 m from pickup (F2); that stop is the very reason Segment 2 is unexempted, and the metered excess-distance charge of $7.99 (F6) was collected on the strength of it.

The exemption asks for cannot shrink the refund to Segment 2 alone: F6 is a single billed excess-distance line (5.67 km × $1.4100 = $7.99) covering both off-route segments, and RD-2 refunds every unexempted segment, arm of which is explained by consent or traffic, so only the metered rate issue in D1 limits recovery, not the number of segments.
Not contested — RD-6 requires a prior upheld route deviation and F21 shows route: 0, so we do not seek flag_account.
Not contested; the record raises no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation (F10–F13), so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation.

We narrow C2 rather than withdraw it: if the judge exempts the 14:10–14:15 segment as the incident-covered substitution under RD-4/RD-5, we accept that segment drops out, and our claim rests on the unmetred 14:17–14:29 segment of F5 plus any 14:10–14:15 excess the incident record does not cover.
Conceded: the fare is metered and the refund base is this trip's own per-km rate of $1.4100/km (F6 = $13.55 ÷ 9.61 km, F9); the driver disputes only which segments count, not the refund mechanism.

The rider's consent claim fails on its own wording: the 'Sure' at 14:02 (F11) answered the driver's 14:01 proposal to 'go round by Cavenagh' (F10), and F4's segment starts at 14:10, so under RD-5 the consent precedes the segment and is at minimum a general route authorization covering the route taken to the destination, which RD-4(a) independently supports via the Orchard Road accident (F18) and band-1 congestion (F15).

Consented: the record contains no road name and no location message tying the driven 14:10–14:15 segment to Cavenagh Road, so it is not exempt as a named-road authorization and the judge may find that segment undetermined rather than covered under RD-5.

RD-4(a) requires the incident to be on the optimal route being replaced and to be listed before the segment starts, and F18 satisfies both (Accident on Orchard Road after Cavenagh Road, 0 m from the route, reported 13:52, two lanes closed) while F15 records band 1 (0–9 km/h) on that same route during 14:00–14:10 — the justification is therefore for the first segment (F4), and the rider's argument that it was 'the old route' is exactly what RD-4(a) asks for.

Not contested as to Segment 2: the rider named no place in F11 and the driver's own statement F14 says he chose the Beach Road shop, and the system record F2 fixes that stop at 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off inside F5 — so the stop does not exempt Segment 2 under RD-3(b)/RD-5.

Accepted in substance: the 14:17–14:29 segment (F5) is the one unexempted detour and the driver's refund exposure is confined to it, but the rider's 'wholly unexplained' framing ignores that the rider asked for a stop she never located (F11), which is why the only exculpatory content for that segment is the driver's statement F14, a claim and not consent.

The rider's own arithmetic already concedes the only contested question: on its reading F4 (the Cavenagh segment) is at worst 'undetermined' and subject to RD-4, so it cannot be summed into a refund as if it were an unexempted detour; the refund base is Segment 2's 2.87 extra km (F5) × $1.4100/km (F6) = $4.05, not $6.66.
Agreed: the $1.08 metered wait time (F7) is collectable on a RydeTAXI trip under RD-3(c) and neither side seeks it.
Agreed: F21 shows the driver's single upheld dispute in 90 days was a no-show with route disputes at 0, so RD-6's repeated-route-deviation condition is not met and no flag_account attaches.
Agreed: F10–F13 contain only a route question, a 'Sure' with a stop request, and 'Ok', all timestamped, with no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 are not engaged.

Refining my own claim rather than withdrawing it: F18 and F15 support the first segment on their own terms, but because no fact names Cavenagh Road for the driven segment (F4), I present that segment as RD-4-exempt with RD-5 consent as a secondary ground, and I no longer press it as a settled named-road exemption.
